results.title: Results
results.description: The releases in the requested window, ordered by date then country. There is no pagination: the provider serves no cursor, so there is nothing to resume from. A response is capped at 2000 releases and the earliest are kept, so a window that comes back with exactly 2000 may have more that were not returned. An unfiltered window reaches that inside a couple of months, since every country together runs to tens of releases a day once the low-impact ones are counted. Narrow the date range, the countries or the impact levels to stay under it.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: The content catalog sources the response was built from, one entry per source. Empty when no catalog source contributed.

usage.description: Tokens the request consumed, per content tier. Present only for API keys billed in tokens.

CommunicationType.title: CommunicationType
CommunicationType.description:
A form an entry takes when it is prose rather than a figure.

The provider flags the two independently and may set both, so a row carries them as
a list rather than choosing between them.

event_datetime.title: Event Datetime
event_datetime.description: When the figure is released, in ISO 8601 format (UTC).

country.title: Country
country.description: Country the release covers. Every value is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code except one: 'EMU', the euro area, which has no ISO code of its own.

impact.description: Expected market impact: NONE, LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH.

period_date.title: Period Date
period_date.description: The period the figure describes, as 'YYYY-MM-DD', which is not when it was released: a December CPI published in January describes December. Read it with 'period_type', which says whether the period is that day, its month or its quarter. Absent on an event with no period, such as a central bank speech.

period_type.description: Granularity of the period: DAY, MONTH or QUARTER. 'NONE' on a release that has no period behind it, such as a central bank speech, where 'period_date' is absent too.

actual.title: Actual
actual.description: The released figure, in full units. Absent until the release happens, which is the usual state for a forward-looking window.

previous.title: Previous
previous.description: The prior period's figure, in full units.

revised.title: Revised
revised.description: The prior period restated, in full units. When present, 'previous' is the figure as first published and this is the corrected one.

ratio_deviation.title: Ratio Deviation
ratio_deviation.description: The provider's own measure of how far the released figure fell from consensus, as a ratio. Published by FXStreet alongside the figures; 'surprise' is the same idea expressed as a signed percentage.

surprise.title: Surprise
surprise.description: How far the released figure fell from the consensus, signed. Read it with 'surprise_unit', which says which of two comparisons produced it: an indicator already published as a percentage is compared by subtraction, in percentage points, and every other indicator relatively, as a percentage of the consensus. Absent when either figure is, and for the relative comparison when the consensus is zero.

surprise_unit.description: What 'surprise' is measured in: 'pp' for percentage points, on an indicator already published as a percentage such as a CPI rate, and '%' for a percentage of the consensus on every other indicator, such as a payroll count. Absent exactly when 'surprise' is. Two surprises cannot be compared without it: -0.2pp and -6.25% describe the same release.

is_better_than_expected.title: Is Better Than Expected
is_better_than_expected.description: Whether the result is good for the economy, as judged by the provider. Direction-aware, unlike 'surprise': a lower unemployment print is a negative surprise and better than expected.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: What the figures are measured in: '%' for a rate, '$' for a monetary value, absent for a count such as jobs.

category.description: The category this indicator is filed under, named the same way the 'categories' filter names one. Absent when the provider filed the event under no category.

communication_types.title: Communication Types
communication_types.description: The prose forms this entry takes: 'REPORT' for a published document, 'SPEECH' for spoken remarks, and both when it is both. Empty on an ordinary data release, which is most of a calendar.

is_all_day.title: Is All Day
is_all_day.description: Whether the event covers the whole day rather than a moment in it. When true, the time of day carried by 'event_datetime' is a convention and not a release time.

is_tentative.title: Is Tentative
is_tentative.description: Whether the timing is provisional. When true, 'event_datetime' is the provider's best estimate of when the figure lands rather than a scheduled time, so do not rely on it to the minute.

actual_is_preliminary.title: Actual Is Preliminary
actual_is_preliminary.description: Whether 'actual' is a first estimate. A preliminary figure is normally restated in a later release.

previous_is_preliminary.title: Previous Is Preliminary
previous_is_preliminary.description: Whether 'previous' is a first estimate rather than a settled figure. This is what a value in 'revised' corrects.

ImpactLevel.title: ImpactLevel
ImpactLevel.description:
How much market movement a release is expected to cause.

The 'impacts' filter takes these names, and each release answers the one it carries.
Case does not matter.

PeriodType.title: PeriodType
PeriodType.description:
The granularity of the period a figure describes.

``NONE`` is how a release with no period behind it is reported, such as a central
bank speech. It arrives as this name rather than as null, and those releases carry no
``period_date`` either.

id.title: Id
id.description: Content catalog identifier of the source.

name.title: Name
name.description: Catalog name of the dataset the data came from.

Source.title: Source
Source.description: A content catalog source that contributed data to a structured-data response.

SurpriseUnit.title: SurpriseUnit
SurpriseUnit.description:
What a surprise figure is measured in.

An indicator already published as a percentage is compared by subtraction, so its
surprise is a number of percentage points; every other indicator is compared
relatively, so its surprise is a percentage of the consensus. Both are
percent-shaped numbers and they are not the same measurement, which is why a row
carries this alongside the figure.

Usage.title: Usage
Usage.description:
Public structured-data usage for a request, aggregated per content tier.

A flat object keyed per content tier, where each key is derived from the
content tier identifier by dropping the ``content-`` prefix and appending
``_tokens`` (e.g. ``corporate-fundamentals`` ->
``corporate_fundamentals_tokens``). It is sparse: only tiers with non-zero
tokens appear, and an absent key means zero tokens for that tier.
